assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from proglucagon processing and incretin action through to durable agonists is a rare full arc from basic hormone biology to a transformative therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large clinical impact on cardiometabolic outcomes and an expanding set of indications. The concept is clear and the impact is now plain.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology and active GLP-1 forms, Drucker the biology and the therapeutic rationale (including GLP-2), and Knudsen the engineering of long-acting agonists. Mojsov's early structural and peptide contributions are credited in the list and are contested in priority terms; a three-person prize leaves her out, which is an unresolved fairness issue.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many large randomized trials and broad independent replication over years of use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, even pressing.
uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution should displace one of the three, and how to treat Habener-type early work, is not clear from the supplied list.
Long-term safety and the full breadth of benefit are still being defined; I have not independently verified recent trial details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that durably eliminate refractory B-cell malignancies opened a new therapeutic modality and cancer immunotherapy field with clear, striking clinical responses.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design and costimulation concepts, June the clinical translation in CLL and ALL, and Rosenberg the adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified T cell foundations. Eshhar and others sit outside this credited set, so the configuration is arguably incomplete; the three here are a defensible but not unique trio.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up from independent groups. Timely, though immunotherapy was recognized in 2018 and the committee may weigh cell therapy as distinct.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among early CAR pioneers is partly disputed and not all are in the credited names.
Late toxicities and durability in solid tumors remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that raise functional SMN protein transformed spinal muscular atrophy from a lethal infant disease into a treatable one. The discovery links an elegant mechanistic insight on SMN2 exon 7 splicing to a clear clinical effect and validates a platform for RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target concept, and Bennett led development of nusinersen at Ionis. A two-person split is natural; the contribution of the Biogen/Ionis clinical teams and others on SMN biology (Melki, Lefebvre) is not captured in this credit set.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with years of real-world and trial data, and independent confirmation of the mechanism. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a drug-development achievement more than a discovery.
The relative weight of the SMN1 gene discovery versus the antisense therapy is not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a previously unknown intracellular signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory biology, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer. Original, clearly defined and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 pathway in yeast and mammals; Walter's group also elucidated Ire1 mechanism and later ISRIB-linked work on integrated stress response. Credit to Ron and Mori for other arms (PERK, ATF6) could be argued, but the two-person core is clean.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and textbook status; Lasker 2014 recognition. The basic discovery is mature, whereas therapeutic translation is still emerging.
uncertainties: Pathway breadth (PERK, ATF6, Ron's role) could complicate allocation; I am not certain how the committee would treat it.
Clinical translation is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with dramatic population-level reductions in disease. The impact is large and demonstrated, and cancer prevention is a strong Nobel theme.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach at the NCI, while Frazer, with Jian Zhou (deceased) and others, contributed early VLP work in Australia, and the zur Hausen link to HPV and cancer is already recognized (2008). Priority between Frazer/Zhou and NCI is a known allocation question, though a three-person split is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Population-level evidence from national vaccination programs, such as reductions in cervical precancer, is strong and independent. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Zhou's death and role in priority claims affect fairness.
Whether the committee sees the 2008 HPV prize as already covering this area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational BCR-ABL inhibition turned CML from a fatal leukemia into a chronic, manageable condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Very high impact and conceptual clarity.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led compound discovery, Druker the clinical development and proof of concept, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. Rowley's and Nowell's cytogenetics and the Witte/Baltimore work on ABL sit outside the credited names, so the configuration omits foundational contributors.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of outcome data and independent replication; Lasker 2009. Mature, perhaps overdue, with the question being whether to credit upstream discoveries.
uncertainties: Upstream credit (Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion) is not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a new method for causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is used across systems and disease models. The method is original and has had a far-reaching impact on brain research.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin, and Deisseroth and Boyden (with Miesenböck's earlier work) established its use in neurons. Six credited names exceed three places, so the choice is contested, and I would not treat my trio as settled.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and replicated for two decades. Recognition is timely, but human therapeutic use is only just emerging, and the prize may be seen as a tool rather than a medical discovery.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck and others is unresolved.
Falls more on methodology than on physiological or medical discovery, a point on which opinions may differ.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role in nutrient-sensitive growth control is a central discovery in cell physiology, with implications for ageing, cancer, immunosuppression and metabolism.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its function; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin was critical to the mechanism and the mammalian target identification was shared by several groups (Sabatini, Sabers, Brabb, Heitman, Movva). Sabatini's inclusion is complicated by documented controversy that I have not independently verified, so I leave him out; that makes the credit incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Very strong independent confirmation and extensive follow-up, though clinical applications (rapalogs) are modest relative to the biology. Timely.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among mTOR discoverers.
The credited trio may not match what the committee would regard as the decisive contributors.
